gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Visitor brings a nostalgic, solder-drawn look, with short ascenders perched over big round bowls and a flat, stencil-like line. And Noto Sans Chakma follows in a friendly sans-serif, its s and c open and uncrowded.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-cham: Retro pixel-glow up top, tall and rounded below. Visitor draws a rope-thin outline with no thick or thin parts, while Noto Sans Cham keeps its c wide open for entry. Visitor is for flair; Noto Sans Cham is for reading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Chunky retro-digital nostalgia, with Visitor's gaping e and short ascenders stamped in lines that never swing from thick to thin. Noto Sans Cherokee settles into a plain sans band of tall letters under short stalks, easy going over a whole page.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-chorasmi: Nostalgic, that's Visitor, squeezed out in one steady toothpaste line. Noto Sans Chorasmian carries a large x-height and short ascenders, its curves stopping short instead of closing, so a long page of sans-serif text moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Visitor has a nostalgic, digital streak, with gaping e shapes and bowls that never swell anywhere along the stroke. Noto Sans Coptic gives the line a dense middle zone; a slightly larger body size would suit it.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-cuneifor: Noto Sans Cuneiform has a lowercase swollen like inflated glass beads, and its e opens up instead of closing its eye, which keeps the sans-serif text friendly. Visitor does the nostalgic pixel-style display work; the body font does the quiet reading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Visitor looks like retro digital signage, with short ascenders over big bowls and counters framed by strokes of matching width. Its strongest quality is the contrast with Noto Sans Deseret, a wide-looking, squat sans-serif.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-devanaga: Noto Sans Devanagari is modest, with an open-tailed g and capitals that blend into the lowercase. Its strongest quality is how Visitor's hairline-free, nostalgic digital strokes stay sturdy and legible at small sizes beside it.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Fine rope seems laid into every Visitor letter, with a gaping e and short ascenders over big bowls. Noto Sans Duployan takes the opposite job, a wide-mouthed a and oversized counters for steady reading, while Visitor handles the nostalgic display.
